name: Naamah
overview: Naamah was a female Ammonitess known as the mother of Rehoboam, who succeeded Solomon as king of Israel. She is identified in Scripture as one of Solomon's foreign wives, representing the Ammonite tribe. No additional personal notes are recorded about her.
namesAndTitles: The name Naamah means 'pleasant' in Hebrew. This proper name is given in 1 Kings 14:21 and reflects a common biblical name without a divine origin indicated.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Naamah as the mother of Rehoboam, Solomon's successor. Beyond this maternal relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Naamah's significance lies in her role as one of Solomon's foreign wives, which Scripture highlights as part of the foreign influences that led Solomon away from exclusive devotion to God. Her presence as an Ammonitess and mother of Rehoboam underscores the challenges faced by the kingdom, contributing to the eventual division that occurred under her son's reign.
